text:
Can you write an email to people who didn't renew their farm share? I run a 30-acre vegetable farm and sell 22-week shares that people pick up every Thursday.

Facts:
- Last year 260 households had a share. 97 didn't renew.
- On July 9 a hailstorm destroyed about half our crops. For the next 6 weeks the boxes had about half the usual amount. We didn't offer refunds or credit, and I sent one short email about it.
- A full share is $540 this year, the same as last year.
- This year we've added a second field on higher ground and put up 2 hail nets over our tomatoes and peppers. That cost $31,000.
- Members can now pause up to 2 weeks and get credit for them.
- Sign-up closes March 15. 52 shares are left.

Under 200 words.

Before I draft, a few questions. These readers paid full price for six weeks of half boxes, got no credit and heard about it in one short email. The answers decide how the email handles that.

1. **Can you offer the people who left anything for last year?** For example a discount, an extra week or some credit. This is the objection they'll have. If the answer is no, the email has to own that plainly rather than talk around it. Either way, I'd rather ask than invent an offer.
2. **Do you know why the 97 left?** Survey answers or replies would tell us whether it was the hail, or the lack of a refund, or how you told people about it. Some may have left for other reasons, like moving or price. That changes what the email should lead with.
3. **What exactly do the new field and the hail nets protect?** Does the higher field cover most crops or only some? If hail hit again, would members be covered better this time? For example, would there be credit for short boxes, or does the new pause credit only apply to weeks members choose? Readers will ask "what happens next time."
4. **How was the rest of last season?** Were the boxes full before July 9 and after the six weeks? That tells readers whether the hail was one bad stretch or a sign of a bad season.
5. **Sign-off and logistics.** I need the farm name, who signs, and the sign-up link or how to sign up. I also need the season start date if you want it in.
6. **Anything they'll find out anyway?** Is there a cost, a limit or a complaint the 97 already know about or will hear from current members? It's better to answer it in the email than have them find it afterwards.

1. No discount or credit for last year. What I can commit to going forward: a credit for any week when weather cuts a box by more than a third, and a short email to members every Thursday of the season. I didn't write more after the hail because I was working 16-hour days to save what was left. I want to say sorry plainly.

2. 41 of the 97 answered a short survey in the fall. 29 of them said they'd come back if we fixed how we handle bad weeks. I don't know about the rest.

3. The hail nets cover only the tomatoes and peppers, not the greens. I don't know exactly how much the higher field protects. I can't promise there will be no crop loss this year. If hail hits again, the new weather credit covers any week a box is cut by more than a third.

4. I don't know.

5. Greenbank Farm, signed by me, Sam Turner. Sign-up is through the link on our website. Pickup is still Thursdays at the farm stand. I don't know the start date.

6. Not that I know of.

Here's the email, at about 185 words.

<final_document>
Subject: We got last summer wrong. Here's what's changed.

After the July 9 hailstorm, your boxes had about half the usual vegetables for six weeks. We didn't offer refunds or credit, and I sent one short email about it. I was working 16-hour days to save what was left, but I should have told you more. I'm sorry.

Of the 41 of you who answered our fall survey, 29 said you'd come back if we fixed how we handle bad weeks. Here's what we've done:

- **A weather credit.** If weather cuts a box by more than a third, you get credit for that week.
- **A short email every Thursday** of the season, so you always know what's happening.
- **A second field on higher ground**, and two hail nets over our tomatoes and peppers, at a cost of $31,000. The nets don't cover the greens, and I can't promise there won't be crop loss. If there is, the credit covers you.
- **Pauses.** You can now pause for up to two weeks and get credit for them.

A full share is still $540, with pickup on Thursdays at the farm stand. Sign up through the link on our website. Sign-up closes March 15, and 52 shares are left.

Sam Turner
Greenbank Farm
</final_document>

- **The survey result:** I used it as the reason for the changes. It tells readers you listened, and the changes answer what they asked for.
- **The higher field:** You don't know how much it protects, so the email doesn't say. It only says the field exists.
- **No credit for last year:** The email says you didn't offer refunds or credit, but it doesn't say whether that still stands. If anyone might expect money back now, you could add "We can't offer credit for last season, but…" before the list of changes.
- **Start date:** I left it out. Add it if you have one before you send.
